newsitem.title: GERMANY: German wheat prices ease in quiet market.
newsitem.headline: German wheat prices ease in quiet market.

text.p: German wheat prices are drifting lower as the export market fails to take off, brokers said on Wednesday.
"There are no reasons for firm prices anywhere in Europe," one said.
Uncertainty about Polish plans to restore customs duties on grains, which would weaken Germany's supply opportunities, also weighed on sentiment. Poland is the most obvious outlet for German wheat.
Domestic consumers were aware of a comfortable supply situation and reluctant to engage in any sales negotiations, brokers added.
Millers refused to accept wheat storage supplements usually added to prices.
Milder temperatures had eased concerns over transport problems and possible damage to winter crops.

The Hamburg grain exchange this week cut its bread wheat price (12.5 percent, 220 Hagberg) free Hamburg by five marks to 275 marks a tonne and also reduced its spot feed wheat by 2.50 marks to 272.50.
Sentiment in other EU countries received a boost last week when Brussels approved 343,000 tonnes of free market wheat for subsidised export, but only 4,000 tonnes of that was German.
Feed wheat demand was reasonably high but attempts to raise domestic prices by citing high sterling-induced prices for competing British supply were unsuccessful.
Barley and rye prices were broadly steady.
Feed barley benefited from firm prices for competing imported protein feeds, but ample supply and expectations barley will be sold into intervention offset possible gains.
In the fob Baltic export market, brokers put normal spot bread wheat (12 percent protein) for second half January at a slightly weaker 285-287.50 marks this week.
The bottom end of higher quality offers was also reduced, with asking prices in a 290-305 range, depending on protein levels.
Fob Baltic barley was quoted at 260-273.50 and fob rye offers were at 254-268 marks.
